#1782. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

🔁 Últim canvi al Girona:➡️ Stuani⬅️ Pyshchur

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

Kabia gets to the byline and intelligently pulls a cross back to Gabriel Jesus, who curls a first-time strike narrowly wide of the far post as Arsenal search for a fifth goal.

Meslier showcases his magnificent reflexes, making a world class save to deny the recently-introduced Ruiz from close-range after he latched onto Martinez’s dangerous delivery.

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

A dominant first-half display in Girona 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ZprG2xLYyj

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

We're making a triple substitution...↩️ Havertz, Hincapie, Gyokeres🔛 Vieira, Salmon, Jesus🔴 0-2 🔵 (32) pic.twitter.com/NtpnUsfAY6

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

#1780. Man United break unwanted record against Roma with 17-minute horror show in Champions League

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 20:55

Manchester United have set yet another unwanted club record in their Champions League showdown with Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday evening.

Searching for their first triumph in any competition since thumping Sabah 4-0 in their opening European clash of the season, the Red Devils got off to an all-too familiar disastrous start.

With just 11 minutes gone, Roma caught Man United cold on the right-hand side, where Matias Soule made his way into the box untracked and calmly slotted home past Senne Lammens.

Just six minutes later, Gian Piero Gasperini's men were given the chance to double their lead from the penalty spot, as Ayden Heaven was penalised for a handball from Soule's next attempt.

Donyell Malen calmly sent Lammens the wrong way, thus providing Roma with a comfortable cushion and writing another dismal chapter of history for Man Utd in the process.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box ? https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES

Having conceded twice inside just 17 minutes, Man United set a new record for the earliest time they have fallen 2-0 down in a home game in a major European competition.

Red Devils fans had already been protesting against the Glazers and INEOS before the game, and disgruntled supporters soon made their frustrations known in a disruptive manner.

Some members of the Old Trafford crowd threw tennis balls onto the pitch behind the Roma goal, and attacker Matheus Cunha took it upon himself to remove them.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are both present at the Theatre of Dreams for the clash with Roma, while anti-Jim Ratcliffe and Glazers chants could also be heard.

The half-time whistle unsurprisingly triggered a cacophony of boos from the home crowd, while Alan Shearer described the Red Devils' performance as "absolutely atrocious" on Amazon Prime.

Man Utd fans are not happy. https://t.co/7yc9jwqz7u

Barring possession, the half-time statistics told the story of a Man United side who were thoroughly dominated by their Italian counterparts, who were full value for their two-goal advantage.

Michael Carrick's men generated a paltry 0.24 Expected Goals to Roma's 1.48, and they could count themselves lucky that their visitors were not further in the ascendancy at the break.

Shortly before the whistle blew, Soule curled a fizzing left-footed strike just wide of the post, as Gasperini's men continuously carved out opportunities against a disjointed Man Utd defence.

Defeat for the Red Devils would mark fourth third in a row across all competitions, and also extend their winless run to 10 matches, although Carrick is expected to remain in charge until the international break regardless of tonight's result.

#1779. Mikel Arteta's mission to conquer his Anfield demons: Why Arsenal boss must overcome psychological damage from his playing days and take the handbrake off as he plots first win at Liverpool, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 08:47 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 11:13 EDT, 1 November 2026

The word 'Anfield' still haunts Mikel Arteta.

It was there, 12 years ago, that the Spaniard suffered a chastening experience after losing 5-1 there as an Arsenal player in February 2014.

In a subsequent interview with Spanish newspaper Marca, Arteta used the term 'pajara' - a Spanish phrase com monly associated with cyclists who suddenly run out of energy - to describe a sensation mirroring mental paralysis. He had been caught up in an Anfield tornado.

'Suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around, the game is passing all over me and I cannot react,' Arteta reflected.

'Everyone is thinking, 'What is he doing?' I cannot react, emotionally, physical. I cannot cope, everything goes fast and I only had that feeling in my career once - and it was at Anfield.'

Such was the impact of that trauma that Arteta felt compelled to bring a slice of Anfield to Arsenal's London Colney base ahead of a league meeting in November 2021.

Mikel Arteta (right) has consistently found life tough when managing away at Anfield

Going to Anfield has become something akin to a hoodoo - and it shows no signs of abating

Arteta surrounded the training pitch with enormous speakers which blared out 'You'll Never Walk Alone' during a training session, in hope the noise would ready his players to tackle the very atmosphere he himself wilted in. It was to no avail.

The Gunners found themselves on the end of a 4-0 drubbing and Arteta on the end of mocking from critics for his alternative methods.

Five years later, Arsenal's away day hoodoo against the Reds has shown no signs of abating.

The north London club's league record against Liverpool away under Arteta reads: six games, three draws, three defeats. Arsenal's most recent league victory there was in September 2012, in which Arteta played in the 2-0 victory.

Their results against Manchester City at the Etihad - their other closest title rivals in recent years - under Arteta are no better either. Seven games have resulted in five defeats and two draws.

In fact, across the 27 Premier League teams Arteta's Arsenal have faced away from home during his seven-year reign, his lowest points-per-game ratios are against Man City (0.29) and Liverpool (0.50).

These matches are more than difficult away trips. They are a test of both Arteta's tactical flexibility and the psycho logical resilience of his team in the face of hostility.

Andoni Iraola's side have appeared to turn a corner in the league after beating the impressive Brighton last weekend. With a cloud of uncertainty hanging over Man City and whether their sanctions for breaching financial rules will be enacted before the season ends, Liverpool may well end up as Arsenal's closest challengers for the title.

Beating Arsenal on Sunday, certainly, would go some way to announcing themselves as true contenders.

Arsenal are champions but they have consistently struggled away against the very best teams

So where have Arteta's Arsenal gone wrong at Anfield and the Etihad Stadium? Well, Arteta's tactical approach has arguably been too cautious in these fixtures for a start.

The 1-0 defeat in August 2025 against Arne Slot's Liverpool smacked of restraint and a concession that a point would be good enough before Dominik Szoboszlai's stunning late free-kick winner.

Arsenal's defensive organisation has long been a major strength under Arteta. He has built his Arsenal from the backline, reinforcing it with excellent back-up options before assessing the forward positions.

Yet, in these high-profile away matches, the pursuit of defensive security can come at the expense of attacking ambition.

There's a big drop in attacking output between when Arsenal face Liverpool at Anfield under Arteta compared with when the Gunners face other league opponents on away turf across the last two seasons.

Possession drops from 56.3 to 43.2 per cent, expected goals from 1.6 to 1.1 and big chances created from 3.1 to 1.8.

The impact of the fervent Anfield atmosphere can't be ignored, either. Ray Parlour understands this better than most, making his Arsenal debut at Anfield in January 1992 aged 18.

The Gunners legend, part of Arsene Wenger's Invincibles side, has a word of advice for the current crop.

'I made my debut there, I know exactly how tough it is to play there. But mentally, you've got to get ready,' Parlour tells Daily Mail Sport.

'For me, the crowd in the first 15 to 20 minutes is always very important at Anfield, because you have to silence them if you can.

Arteta's attack routinely suffers as he seeks defensive solidity in the toughest away games

Arsenal are very strong when they score first but slow starts have proven their Achilles heel

'You've got to start on the front foot, put them under pressure, and I think they can leak goals, Liverpool. To try score that first goal is always important.

'We know defensively Arsenal are a very strong side, so if they go and get that first goal, then they might have a good afternoon there.'

Parlour raises a pertinent point. Arsenal's slow starts at Anfield have left themselves with a mountain to climb. Of the 26 league games Arsenal won last season, they scored first in 24 of those matches. Whereas in the six away matches against Liverpool under Arteta, the Gunners have taken time to getting going.

More shots (from 27 to 30) and an increased xG (from 3.2 to 3.5) were registered in the second period compared to the first half in those games.

Arsenal need to start quicker - and be more clinical, too. At the Emirates, Arteta's men have struck 10 goals against Liverpool, but just six at Anfield despite creating more big chances at Anfield (1.8 per away game vs 1.1 per home game).

Parlour references Arsenal's 3-0 pummelling at Brighton last month as a key example. Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler admitted telling his players to 'win the small battles first' and that's exactly what they did.

'Win the first header, win the first tackle, win the first throw in, win the first corner,' revealed Hurzeler when asked about his pre-match message to his players. The Gunners can use this as a lesson to overcome their bogey team.

'Look, they're champions. They've got to play in all different sort of atmospheres,' explains Parlour.

'There's a lot of experienced players out there, so you know what to expect.

Arteta played in Arsenal's last league win at Anfield - a 2-0 victory 14 years ago against Brendan Rodgers' Liverpool. He will look to end that streak as a manager on Sunday

Former Arsenal midfielder Ray Parlour wants to see a bravery that can help navigate the storm

'It's going to be a tough place to play, but you've just got to go there and play your game. Individuals win their battles, which is very important in football.

'You see Brighton when they turned over Arsenal, they won their battles that day, so you've got to make sure you get one over on the players you're playing against.

Ultimately, if Arteta is to banish the Anfield demons that have lingered for 12 years, Arsenal must arrive with the courage to impose themselves from the first whistle - and the resilience to withstand the inevitable storm. Only then can the Spaniard finally rewrite a story that has haunted him for so long.

#1778. PSG break incredible Champions League scoring record in 17-minute Villarreal rout

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 21:03, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 21:15

Paris Saint-Germain broke an outrageous Champions League goalscoring record in their first-half rout of Villarreal on Tuesday evening.

Luis Enrique's men travelled to La Ceramica aiming to make it four wins from four in the 2026-27 tournament after getting the better of Slovan Bratislava, Manchester City and Barcelona in the opening three rounds.

Les Parisiens got off to the best start imaginable against their La Liga counterparts, as Joao Neves broke the deadlock inside nine minutes before Desire Doue doubled the lead in the 12th.

Senny Mayulu added a third for PSG less than a minute after Villarreal had kicked off again, before Fabian Ruiz got in on the act with the visitors' fourth just a few moments later.

Ruiz's strike hit the back of the net with 16 minutes and two seconds on the clock, seeing PSG set a new record for the fastest time to score four goals in a single Champions League game.

It’s ANOTHER goal for PSG ? Fabián Ruiz with a brilliant finish to make it four ? ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/kN6lYvEWOr

After successfully completing their quest for back-to-back Champions League titles in 2025-26, PSG seemed to have lost their golden touch at the start of the current campaign.

Enrique's men edged out Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup but then failed to win any of their first three Ligue 1 fixtures, taking just two points from the first nine on offer.

However, the 6-1 crushing of Slovan Bratislava sparked a major revival for Les Parisiens, who have known nothing but wins since then, prevailing in nine straight games in all tournaments.

PSG's first half against Man City was almost unheard of from a visiting team at the Etihad, while putting four past Barcelona also underlined their credentials as genuine three-peat candidates.

The reigning European champions have also scored at least twice in eight of their nine victories in that sequence, and few would bet against them retaining their crown for the third year running.

16:02 - Le Paris Saint-Germain vient d'établir le record de l'équipe la plus rapide à inscrire quatre buts en Ligue des Champions (16 minutes et 2 secondes). Survol. https://t.co/9XDC7SHs7B

Things got even better for PSG early in the second half against Villarreal, as Ruiz bagged his second of the night - and the champions' fifth - in the 50th minute.

Even if Les Parisiens do not net again at La Ceramica, they will be sitting on a staggering 19 goals from their first four games of the competition, an average of over 4.5 per match.

If Enrique's men make it all the way to the final while carrying on at their current scoring rate - and assuming they progress straight to the last 16 rather than going through the playoffs - they would end the competition with approximately 86 goals.

Such a total would obliterate the current single-season record for goals in the Champions League, jointly held by PSG themselves and the 1999-00 Barcelona team, who scored 45 each.

Much sterner tests are to come for PSG, and for the holders to keep scoring 4+ goals a game would be unheard of, but their own record is very much there for the taking.

Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Chambers, Kerkez; Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Morrison, Isak, Ngumoha.Substitutes: Woodman, Davies, Chiesa, Jones, Elliott, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Abe, Ramsay, Scanlon, McConnell, Koumas, Ndiaye, Wright, Sonni-Lambie.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#1775. Bayer Leverkusen vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 03 Nov 2026 21:33

Bayer Leverkusen's perfect Europa League record comes under threat again when Marseille travel to face them at BayArena on Thursday.

The hosts boast three wins from three in Europe so far, and their tally of nine points means they are second in the league-phase table, whereas visitors Marseille are third last in 34th place with no points.

Leverkusen's previous match in the Europa League was a 2-0 victory against OFI Crete on October 22, and they have now scored eight goals and kept three clean sheets in the tournament.

Carles Martinez's side have since played three games in all competitions, losing twice in the Bundesliga while beating Nurnberg 5-2 in the DFB-Pokal on October 28.

Their latest result was a 4-2 league defeat against Stuttgart on Saturday, and that loss left them sixth in the top flight with 13 points after eight matchweeks.

Die Werkself's clash with Stuttgart ended their perfect record at home, with the club having won their first five games at BayArena in 2026-27.

In their six outings at the stadium, Leverkusen conceded seven goals, though they kept three clean sheets in their opening three matches at the ground.

Marseille's campaign has been far from straightforward, though they have at least started to find form in Ligue 1 given they have won their past four fixtures in the division.

The French side are sixth in the table with 15 points from a possible 27, but only three points separate them from second-placed Lille and five points from first-placed Paris Saint-Germain.

While head coach Bruno Genesio came under immense pressure at the start of the season following an opening stretch of five losses and one triumph, he has since overseen four wins from six games.

Les Olympiens scored 13 goals in those six matches, though they conceded on seven occasions and kept just two clean sheets.

Marseille's form on their travels has been poor for some time considering they have been beaten in seven of their past 10 away contests, and they have lost four of their six away clashes this season.

Bayer Leverkusen form (all competitions):

Bayer Leverkusen are dealing with an injury crisis in attack, with forwards Eliesse Ben Seghir, Martin Terrier, Christian Kofane and Moussa Diaby all ruled out.

The hosts may have no other option but to field Lucas Vazquez, Ibrahim Maza and Afonso Moreira behind striker Patrik Schick.

With right-back Guela Doue still set for a few weeks on the treatment table, former Liverpool defender Jarell Quansah is the obvious option on the right.

As for Marseille, left-back Emerson Palmieri avoided a serious injury against Toulouse on Sunday, but perhaps Ulisses Garcia will be used on Thursday.

Midfielders Tochukwu Nnadi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Himad Abdelli are set to play together, and they will be expected to support striker Amine Gouiri.

Bayer Leverkusen possible starting lineup:

Leverkusen may have struggled for consistency in domestic football, but they have been excellent in Europe so far.

Despite their injury woes, the hosts should still believe they can beat Marseille, who have rarely travelled well in recent months.

#1774. Carlos Baleba injury: How many Man Utd games could he miss?

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 21:37

Manchester United were dealt a devastating new injury blow against Roma, as Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury in the Champions League encounter.

The former Brighton & Hove Albion man was given the nod alongside Kobbie Mainoo in the centre of the park against the Giallorossi, but the Red Devils were soon overrun.

Matias Soule's strike and Donyell Malen's penalty put Roma 2-0 up inside just 17 minutes, seeing Man United break an unwanted club record for the quickest time to concede two goals in a European home game.

Supporters - who were already voicing their disapproval towards INEOS and the Glazers - temporarily halted the game by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch, before booing the players off at half time.

Michael Carrick's men generated just 0.24 Expected Goals in the first half, but they quickly found themselves in behind in the second period, only for the attack to break down in painful circumstances.

Baleba looks distraught as he limps off ? #mufc https://t.co/TM99RzCjYQ

Baleba found himself one-on-one with Roma goalkeeper Devis Vazquez at a tight angle, but as the Cameroonian was bearing down on goal, he pulled up clutching his hamstring before getting a shot or a pass off.

Vazquez gratefully collected the ball while Baleba collapsed in agony in the goal, and the 22-year-old trudged off to be replaced by Youri Tielemans in the 51st minute.

Baleba gingerly walked to the tunnel with a member of the medical team as he prepares to undergo further assessment, having been dealt another setback in his fledgling Man United career.

The midfielder's Red Devils debut was initially delayed due to an ankle injury, as he did not make his first appearance for Man United until October 10 against Tottenham Hotspur.

Baleba has started each of Man United's last three Premier League games, though, and he was making his second European start of the campaign against Roma.

Some hamstring issues simply prove to be tightness or scares, which can heal in a few days, but Baleba's actions were indicative of a true hamstring strain.

However, if the 22-year-old has only suffered a Grade 1 injury, he could be back in a couple of weeks, meaning he would only miss the visit of Aston Villa on November 8 and return against Liverpool on November 22 following the international break.

A Grade 2 problem could rule Baleba out for around six weeks, though, meaning he would also be unavailable for fixtures against Sporting Lisbon and Brentford before the end of the month, as well as Newcastle United, Coventry City, RB Leipzig and Crystal Palace in the first half of December.

A Grade 3 injury - a complete tear - would require a three-month recovery period, keeping Baleba sidelined until early February and forcing him to miss crunch clashes with Arsenal (December 20), Bayern Munich (January 20) and Liverpool (January 23).

#1773. Everyone loves a good comedy

The Premier League continues to amuse this season, with Man Utd’s troubles continuing after a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford yesterday. It probably spells the end of Michael Carrick as manager, which is a bit of a shame. I loved his work. Up there with Ruben Amorim and Ruud van Nistelrooy for me. Legend, in my opinion.

Obviously though, United’s problems run deeper than the man on the touchline. The dressing room is a toxic mess, which is quite funny because that’s the kind of thing Sir Jimmy Ratcliffe is an expert in given his position at INEOS – one of the UK’s great polluters. Still, whatever happens at Man Utd, however he continues to ruin internal morale by installing soup kitchens and firing staff like they’re not people worth a moment’s consideration, I guess he can just enjoy life as bigoted old tax-exile in Monaco, wondering why it is that he feels ‘his’ country isn’t what it used to be as he avoids contributing to society by paying his fair share.

I saw a story the other the day in the Athletic about how 72 year old Ratcliffe once went to the physio room to offer players advice on stretching because he’d run the London Marathon. If that doesn’t tell you exactly how dysfunctional that club is, nothing will. Except, of course, for the results on the pitch, the way they play, their position in the table, and the fact that senior players are basically saying ‘F*ck this! I have to go public’ in post-match interviews. But honestly, imagine Stan Kroenke at London Colney giving Viktor Gyokeres advice on how to hold it up, because he’d spent years holding up objections to one of his massively obscene land deals.

I can’t say I have a lot of time for either Lisandro Martinez or Bruno Fernandes, and they will probably become targets for being outspoken. Maybe they were wrong to do it, maybe as captain Fernandes is entirely the wrong kind of character when your club is in this kind of a situation, but it still speaks to the mess that exists on and off the pitch that they’ve said what they’ve said. Yes, it’s very, very entertaining for all of us, but in a purely objective sense, it says a lot.

I remember when Ralf Rangnick was boss there for a while, and he was roundly pilloried because results weren’t good, but he was spot on four or five years ago when he spoke about how the place needed an entire rebuild. I think he said something like it required open heart surgery, and he was absolutely right. All this time later, that operation is still required, but they have a xenophobic egomaniac in charge who would happily deport most of his playing staff if they weren’t talented footballers, and who continues to oversee bad decision after bad decision. Most of the club is still owned by the Glazers who never gave a shit anyway, and as Arsenal fans we know this kind of ownership structure is no good. Now they’ll probably just repeat the cycle where some ex-player will come in on an interim basis, get a few half decent results, and that wobbly-mouthed halfwit Rio Ferdinand will do a giddy dance on live TV about giving him a six year contract because he ‘knows the club’. Which is probably what they’ll do.

Welcome to the hot-seat Darren Fletcher/John O’Shea/Phil Jones/Henning Berg/David May/Alan Smith (the evil blue-lipped one)/Nani. Oh, please, give it to Phil Neville. Listening to Gary tie himself in knots every week on Sky would be amazing. Surely a reward for all us having to listen to him for all these years. Come on universe, you owe us this at least.

I saw a clip of a renowned Man Utd streamer going mad during their humiliating defeat at home yesterday, scornfully saying ‘But it’s Bournemouth! It’s Bournemouth!’, which tells you plenty. Anyone who has watched Bournemouth over the last few seasons would understand that even with a new manager in charge, they are a really good side with good players who can hurt you. The arrogance, the hubris, to think that just because their ground only holds a fraction of the capacity of Ancient Trafford, you are entitled to win the game.

I’m not saying he is part of the problem, per se, but if that level of delusion exists within their fanbase despite all the evidence they’ve had presented to them – right in front of their very eyes! – then it probably tells you something about the job that club needs to do. Thankfully for all of us, they appear to have a collection of people in charge thoroughly incapable of doing that. Sir Jimmy might brilliant at pumping petrochemical run-off into the atmosphere and poisoning wildlife, but he seems to be something of a footballing idiot. And quite hilariously, their current chief executive is a man called Omar Berrada, who used to work at Man City where two of his job titles between 2011 and 2015 were ‘Head of International Business Development’ and ‘Director of Partnership Sales’. What an interesting timeline that is, eh?!

I know we all have our issues with Arsenal, and we’ve been through some stuff over the years, but on this Monday morning as we begin a new week, let’s take a moment to be thankful for where we are right now. One decision can absolutely change the trajectory of your football club, and for us that was the appointment of Mikel Arteta. Reading lately that other options were considered ahead of him gave me a shudder, because we absolutely would not be in the same rude health if we’d gone down those particularly avenues.

Which is to say, the very best of luck to the Steve Bruce – Gary Pallister dream team.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now, but we will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on today. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around noon or so. Until then, have a good one.

#1770. A chance for rotation and rest as we face Fleetwood Town

We’re in EFL Cup action this evening, taking on Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium (not that one). Tonight’s opposition sit 18th in League Two, and this will surely influence Mikel Arteta’s team selection. There are players I just do not want to see this evening. Not just from the start, but not in the squad at all.

The likes of Declan Rice, Gabriel, Ezri Konsa, Martin Odegaard have all played a lot and could use a night off, and I would also include the two wide players we have fit – Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. With injuries to Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis, we’re very light in that area of the pitch, and we do not need to risk them in a game like this. There’s still plenty of scope for rotation, and there are some senior players who could use some minutes, as well as an opportunity to fill out the bench with Academy lads.

You imagine we’ll see starts for Kepa, Martin Zubimendi (assuming his nose isn’t too sore after the weekend), Cristhian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, maybe Jurrien Timber, Myles Lewis-Skelly, and possibly Bruno Guimaraes, but also it’s an opportunity for Marli Salmon and Max Dowman again, both of whom started in the last round against Ipswich. Dowman played centrally that evening, in the Odegaard role, and got two goals, but I wonder if tonight he might be used out wide as we rest Madueke.

After that, young players like Ife Ibrahim and Theo Julienne will be hoping for minutes to add to the ones they picked up in the last round, while forwards like Ceadach O’Neill and Igor Tyjon might fancy their chances of being included. This is a kind draw ahead of a weekend trip to Anfield, and with Liverpool playing Chelsea tomorrow night, it’s an opportunity for the manager to ease the burden on the guys who have played a lot as well as giving the next generation a chance too.

I think we’ll also see Viktor Gyokeres up front, and the Swedish international could really do with a goal. He’s on a barren streak (in club terms at least), that stretches back to May 2nd, and it’s now 15 games without a goal. Even though his minutes have been a bit scant this season, that’s a record that’s hanging over him and one he’ll want to put right. A goal, or goals, against a League Two side in this competition will always have that little caveat applied, but it ought to be a real opportunity for him to build a little goalscoring confidence, so fingers crossed he can do exactly that.

Speaking about tonight’s game, Arteta said:

Every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve to do that, and then try to win and try to play better than them.

So, let’s see how it plays out later on, kick off is 20.00 in this part of the world.

Elsewhere, while I find the concept of individual awards in football completely counter-intuitive to what makes the game as compelling as it is, I did want to mention Bukayo Saka winning the Socrates Award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony last night. The official website reports that: “Bukayo and his family have worked with multiple charities, including long-term projects with Big Shoe, providing medical care and humanitarian aid for children and families in need in London and around the world.”

And yet, they are often held up as an example of people who earn too much for doing too little. I remember during Covid, politicians singled out football players as those who should set an example by taking wage cuts or making charity donations or supporting the health services, while ignoring those who – less publicly – earn far, far more. But as we can see here, someone like Bukayo Saka (and he’s far from alone too), uses what his talent has provided to help others, and while I’m sure he doesn’t do it for awards or recognition, this spotlight on what he does can help the causes he supports.

This is an individual award worth highlighting, and you can see the ceremony and his speech about it below.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for now. #1769. Benfica vs Lech Poznan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 03 Nov 2026 21:44, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 21:59

Benfica will look to maintain their perfect start to the 2026-27 Europa League league phase campaign when they welcome Lech Poznan to the Estadio da Luz on Thursday evening.

Marco Silva's side sit top of the 36-team table with nine points from three matches, while the Polish champions are down in 32nd place with just one point, leaving Niels Frederiksen's men with a difficult task against one of the competition's early pace-setters.

Benfica have made an impressive start to the league-phase campaign, winning their opening three Europa League matches against AC Milan (2-0), Celtic (4-1) and Omonia (4-1) in their most recent continental outing.

Those results have left the Lisbon outfit at the top of the Europa League standings as one of just five teams to have won all three of their opening fixtures, while their 10 goals also make them the competition's highest-scoring side.

Silva's men have been in excellent form across all competitions, winning 14 of their last 15 matches, with their only defeat coming against Porto in the league Classico on September 20, before responding with six consecutive victories.

Although last weekend's 1-0 home success over Alverca - secured by Vangelis Pavlidis' 51st-minute penalty - was the only match in that winning run in which Benfica failed to score more than once, it also marked their first clean sheet in five outings and kept them second in the Primeira Liga table, five points off the summit.

Benfica will now turn their attention back to Europe, where another victory would strengthen their position in the race for automatic qualification to the knockout stages, and they can draw confidence from a home record of nine wins in 10 matches (D1) this season.

That includes victories in all four of their Europa League fixtures at Da Luz across the qualifying rounds and league phase, scoring at least three goals in each and finding the net 18 times while conceding just three.

Lech, meanwhile, arrive in Lisbon with a far less convincing European record after suffering 4-0 defeats to Crystal Palace and Bayer Leverkusen, though they did claim their first point of the league phase in a 1-1 home draw against Sunderland in their most recent continental outing, with Leo Bengtsson scoring a 70th-minute equaliser.

Having conceded nine goals in the league phase, the Kolejorz have the joint-second-worst defensive record in the competition, with only bottom-placed Ararat-Armenia shipping more, while no side in the competition has found the net fewer times than the Polish champions’s one strike in the competition this term.

Frederiksen's team have endured an inconsistent run across all competitions in recent weeks, winning four of their seven matches since returning from the October international break, a period that also saw them eliminated from the Polish Cup to lower-division Siarka Tarnobrzeg.

Lech’s domestic form has been far more encouraging, though, with last weekend's 3-1 victory over Wisla Krakow marking their fifth consecutive league win, leaving the Kolejorz three points clear at the top of the Ekstraklasa table after collecting 31 points from a possible 36 this season.

However, the Poznan-based club face a much tougher test on Thursday, having lost both of their previous meetings with Benfica in the 2020-21 Europa League group stage, suffering a 4-2 defeat at home before falling 4-0 at the Estadio da Luz.

Benfica are expected to be without Leandro Barreiro, who faces around two months on the sidelines with a thigh injury, while Enzo Barrenechea remains doubtful as he continues to recover from a knee problem.

Dodi Lukebakio was forced off during the second half of last weekend's victory over Alverca, although reports suggest the issue is not serious, while Rafa Silva remains in contention to return to the starting lineup on the right side of the attack.

Pavlidis has scored in each of his last four appearances for Benfica and also found the net in both of his starts in this season's Europa League league phase, making the Greek striker one to watch.

Lech will definitely be without Ali Gholizadeh, who is recovering from an ACL injury, Joao Moutinho, who has a broken foot, and Alex Douglas, who is sidelined with an ankle problem.

Meanwhile, Wojciech Monka and Mikael Ishak are still nursing muscle problems, while Allahyar Sayyadmanesh is working his way back from a hamstring problem.

Trubin; Bah, Araujo, Lenglet, Dahl; Palhinha, Aursnes; Rafa Silva, Sudakov, Prestianni; Pavlidis

Lis; Pereira, Skrzypczak, Yegbe, Gurgul; Kozubal, Murawski; Walemark, Rodriguez, Hakans; Bengtsson

The difference in quality between the two sides has been reflected in their respective European campaigns, and Benfica's impressive attacking form makes them strong favourites to claim another victory.

The Portuguese side have also been particularly difficult to contain at the Estadio da Luz this season, and they should have enough to secure a comfortable win.

#1768. O'Neill admits new signings are struggling with demands of being a Celtic player after dispiriting loss at Falkirk

Published: 11:08 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 11:21 EDT, 1 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill admitted his summer recruits need to prove that they have the character and quality to handle the pressure of playing for the club.

The league leaders went down 2-0 at Falkirk on Sunday afternoon – their sixth defeat in their last 10 in all competitions – as they missed the chance to extend their advantage at the top of the Premiership table to seven points.

First-half strikes from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser had the Bairns ahead at the break, and despite peppering Scott Bain’s goal in the second period, the visitors were unable to find a response.

When it was put to O’Neill that some new members of his squad are still struggling to meet the club’s high expectations, he said: ‘Absolutely. You have to cope with the pressure to be a player.

‘Tommy Burns said it might be easier to play against Celtic than for Celtic but hopefully we have enough in the dressing room and players who have been big winners.

‘When you ask managers sometimes you think the best team is the one that has won convincingly, but there are a number of players who have arrived.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill was unhappy with his team's defending at Falkirk

‘You can think someone is doing well in training but the only place to find where players fit is out there.

‘We’re not used to losing a lot of games. We were in a much worse position this time last year so we have to buckle down and win a game and win a game in Europe. Thursday [against Besiktas in the Europa League] is a big game and then the following Sunday is massive before we go into the international break.

‘We need to sort out a few things. I was asked about confidence. If you take Kasper [Hogh], he wanted to get a goal after some time.

‘Something might fall for him but it’s not just that something might fall for you. You have to work at it which is something us as a team and the players in particular need to do.’

O’Neill bemoaned the defensive lapses that allowed Falkirk to open up a two-goal cushion, but saw enough in his team’s performance in the attacking third to give him confidence that things will soon start clicking.

‘I’m naturally disappointed to have lost the game,’ he said. ‘We had a lot of chances. Their goalie was magnificent but naturally we’ve lost so I’m very disappointed.

Callum McGregor looks frustrated as Celtic are made to suffer in Falkirk

‘The goals were very poor from our viewpoint. We didn’t clear it for the first one then we let someone run through and pick his spot for the second. We had some really great chances we just weren’t able to convert.

‘At half-time I thought we were still in the game. I thought we’d played decent stuff. If you concede a magnificent goal you take it in your stride.

‘When you concede a bad goal, which from any viewpoint was a poor goal, then it’s tough to come back then the goalie makes some saves and it’s frustrating.

‘Despite mistakes at the back we had enough chances to get back.

‘We have conceded some poor goals and haven’t kept a clean sheet for some time which is the essence of a championship team, but we’re still top and we need to address it and that’s the way out of it.

‘We scored seven against Hearts which isn’t that long ago. I just thought the goalie had a magnificent game and we should have scored a number in each half.

‘When you don’t it becomes frustrating. We have to address that we were conceding. Hopefully we can still do that. It’s still a long season.’

#1766. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1765. Romano: Another renewal and two targets – the moves for Milan after Pulisic’s extension

AC Milan are looking to build on their derby win and surge up the table, while the management continue to plan for the future.

Important developments came in the past few days, starting with the renewal of Christian Pulisic’s contract until 2031 which was made official on Friday, the day before he opened the scoring against Inter with a header.

On the night of the game, Fabrizio Romano confirmed that an agreement in principle had been reached with Markus Krösche to become the new Head of Football. It also seems that the extension of Adrien Rabiot – another derby hero – isn’t far away either.

Romano gave an update last night in a video on his YouTube channel, explaining what the planned moves are for Milan during what is a potentially decisive stage in their project.

“There’s work to be done and construction to be done, even in terms of contracts. The next player to be renewed will be Rabiot. AC Milan is working hard on this signing. Rabiot is the symbol of AC Milan’s intelligent operations. The club wants to secure him,” he said (via MilanNews).

“Then there’s the transfer market. Milan wants to present themselves with confidence. The defender they didn’t sign in the summer could arrive in January. I mentioned Gonçalo Inacio’s name last week and I’ll continue to mention it.

“He remains a highly sought-after player. There are other options, but the defender is a key issue for Milan. It won’t end here. I expect a move in attack, and Milan will certainly do something other than the defender.”
